review.scope: Work-specific source-body sampling, exact structure and provenance checks. No exhaustive human approval or global registry change.

decisions.author: John Gill

sixAnchorEvidence.finding: Divine authority; perfect rule and standard of faith/practice.
Three persons in the unity of the divine essence.
Divine Son with human nature, two natures in one person.
Voluntary substitution in sinners place, satisfaction, divine-human Mediator.
Same real body raised that died, physical wounds and handling cited.

sixAnchorEvidence.anchor: Grace and faith apart from works
sixAnchorEvidence.finding: Free grace, Christ righteousness, faith receiving rather than moral-law works. Preserve Gill distinctions about decree, actual justification and manifested justification.

newWorkEvidence.finding: Historic Ezra/Cyrus/Jeremiah exposition sampled; conservative author identification consistent with Gill. Selected JSON witness, not print collation.

limits: Underlying print impression and transcription lineage unresolved; no exact critical/unabridged edition claim.
API English body wrongly declares rtl in metadata; render English by actual language, preserve source field.
Chronicles contains empty/pointer-only chapters; these are not filled sustained-exegesis gaps.
Historical covenant, eschatological, gospel-offer and pre-faith justification claims stay attributed; no uniform Baptist position inferred.
Ancient rabbis, polemical quotations and alternative interpretations are not independent endorsed teaching.

decisions.author: Benjamin Keach

sixAnchorEvidence.locator: Held short confession: Trinity; Scriptures; Christ Mediator; humiliation/exaltation; justification; resurrection
sixAnchorEvidence.finding: Explicit six-anchor confidence, including one essence/three persons, two natures/one Christ, satisfaction in our place, third-day resurrection, faith alone and authoritative Scriptures.

newWorkEvidence.locator: Four offered volumes; all 47 division opening passages inspected in actual EPUBs
newWorkEvidence.finding: Sustained biblical exposition, doctrine and application; Luke 15 prodigal sequence, Matthew 3 repentance, and Luke 18 justified publican sampled. Reuse existing III.

limits: Modern EPUB arrangement has 1858 Volume I title page and 1701 author preface; no historical two-volume set identity substituted.
Eight specific passage-label/citation defects recorded; original preserved.
Source-specific typology and eschatology remain attributed interpretations, not automatically canonical relationships.
Modern packaging/editorial material remains separately identified; no redistribution to external AI datasets or public app.

decisions.author: Matthew Henry

sixAnchorEvidence.locator: A Method for Prayer, preface and Scripture-shaped prayer method
sixAnchorEvidence.finding: Scripture provides the rule/language of prayer and interpretation.
Distinct Father, Son, Holy Spirit; one divine Godhead.
Eternal divine Word made flesh; born of woman.
Christ suffered in sinners place as sin offering and satisfied divine justice; actual new chapter inspected.
Third-day resurrection, Christ living again, Holy One did not see corruption, bodily resurrection 1 Corinthians 15.

sixAnchorEvidence.locator: Held Volume I gen-xvi.xhtml: Genesis 15:6 exposition
sixAnchorEvidence.finding: Explicit justification by faith without law works; Abraham not justified by his good works. Confidence comes from inspected body, not publisher affiliation.

limits: Held Volume I title appears whole-Bible but body is Genesis-Deuteronomy only. Completing OT does not complete six-volume whole Bible.
Henry Genesis 17 gen-xviii.xhtml makes circumcision give way to baptism: explicitly retain non-Baptist covenant/ordinance difference; not default Baptist teaching.
Volumes V and posthumous contributor-written VI deferred; contributors require their own admission review.
Historic chronology, typology and pastoral applications are attributed interpretations.
Publisher front matter and indexes are not original-author doctrine; CCEL permits private educational use, not blanket republication.
